title: Quoting Ted Sanders
body: In general, LLM performance is incredibly multidimensional. There's no guarantee of a fixed ordering where the model that is best at math is also the model that's best at jokes. Despite that complexity, much of the variation in performance is explained by just a single variable: model size. In general, models that are bigger will (a) be more performant / reliable, (b) cost more per token, and (c) have better recall of esoteric facts. As you note, our models are ordered: Luna < Terra < Sol < Astra [ ... ] These days, version number signifies a few things at once: the order of release, the relationship to other releases, and the magnitude of improvement. So something like 6.1 would indicate it was launched after 5.6, may share some similarities to other 6.1 models in terms of training data / personality (which is why it's not 5.7), and isn't a giant enough leap to merit the headlines and expectations that would come with a 7. — Ted Sanders , explaining OpenAI's model naming conventions Tags: generative-ai , gpt , openai , ai , llms , ted-sanders

README 節錄：# print-my-profile-pic Star this repo to have your GitHub profile picture framed, printed out on my receipt printer, and stuck to my wall. That's it! > [!TIP] > If you give a one-time sponsorship of any amount beforehand, your profile picture will be printed in a **special frame**. ## How's it work? GitHub allows you to create webhooks for specific events on your repos, I've set one up for starring this project. When that happens, a payload is POSTed to a Cloudflare tunnel domain, which leads to a PHP script running on a Raspberry Pi that's sitting on my desk. From the inbound request, you can gleen info about the person who starred the repo, like their display name and avatar URL. The script takes their profile picture, renders it behind a cut-out of a photo frame, and then adds some other info I thought should be included in each receipt. The RPi is connected to an Epson TM-T88IV thermal receipt printer via USB, and the PHP script uses my go-to escpos-php library to format the receipt data and send it off to the printer. ## But why? It sounded fun when my friend Sam mentioned it. That's pretty much it! ## What now? I'll periodically update this README with a picture of the pinboard I've dubbed the "Hall of Frame" as pictures get added to it. Want to add a new frame? Send in a PR!

title: mirkobrombin/raven
body:
A Windows your apps recognize.

README 節錄： A Windows your apps recognize. Website and documentation Raven runs Windows applications on Linux. You install them with their own installers, the same ones you would use on a PC, and they start: no virtual machine, no winetricks, no DLL overrides. The program's code runs directly on your CPU, inside a sandbox where it cannot reach Linux. Every call it makes to the system is answered by Raven, which plays the part of the Windows kernel and its services: processes and threads, files, the registry, windows and input.
